story.iWant: summaries to be generated as markdown files in addition to JSON
story.soThat: I can easily read and review summaries without parsing JSON
story.tasks:
- **Task 1: Verify existing markdown generation in SilverIOManager** (AC: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) - Review `dagster_project/resources/io_managers.py` lines 278-331 - Verify `_handle_output_summary` saves both .json and .md files - Verify `_generate_markdown_summary` creates proper format - Confirm both success and failure paths generate markdown - Check that title field is populated correctly (may need enhancement)
- **Task 2: Enhance markdown format if needed** (AC: 2, 7) - Extract title from summary metadata if available - Review markdown template for readability - Ensure metadata footer is well-formatted - Add any missing fields (author, published_date, etc.) if relevant
- **Task 3: Create integration tests for markdown generation** (AC: 6) - Add test to `tests/integration/test_silver_summarization.py` or create new test file - Test 1: Verify both JSON and markdown files created for successful summary - Test 2: Verify markdown file created for failed summary - Test 3: Verify markdown content structure (title, URL, summary, footer) - Test 4: Verify same hash used for both .json and .md filenames - Test 5: Verify markdown is human-readable (basic format checks) - Mark all tests with `@pytest.mark.integration`
- **Task 4: Manual verification and sample review** (AC: 7) - Run silver_summaries asset on sample data - Manually inspect generated markdown files - Verify formatting, readability, and completeness - Document sample output in completion notes
- **Task 5: Run all tests and quality checks** (AC: 6) - Run `uv run pytest` - verify all tests pass - Run `make check` - verify format, lint, typecheck pass - Verify no regressions in existing tests

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: | AC # | Criterion | Verification | |------|-----------|--------------| | AC1 | `SilverIOManager` saves summaries as both `.json` and `.md` files | Both file types exist in artifacts/silver/summaries/ | | AC2 | Markdown format includes title, URL, summary content, and metadata footer | Markdown structure verified in tests | | AC3 | Markdown files stored alongside JSON in `artifacts/silver/summaries/` | Directory structure verified | | AC4 | Filename uses same full hash as JSON (e.g., `{hash}.md` and `{hash}.json`) | Filenames match with 64-char SHA256 hash | | AC5 | Failed summaries also get markdown format showing error details | Error markdown format verified | | AC6 | Integration test verifies both JSON and markdown files are created | Test passes | | AC7 | Sample markdown output is human-readable and well-formatted | Manual review confirms readability |

doc.title: Architecture Documentation - DeepRock
doc.snippet: Silver Layer stores cleaned, validated, and enriched data ready for consumption in artifacts/silver/ with subdirectories: extracted_content/ (cleaned content) and summaries/ (LLM-generated summaries in JSON + markdown). Silver characteristics: business logic applied, quality validated, enriched with metadata, application-ready format.

doc.title: Architecture Documentation - DeepRock
doc.snippet: File Naming Within Directories uses format {full_sha256_hash}.{extension} - example 64-char hash. Note replaces current truncated SHA256[:16] approach (64 chars vs 16 chars). Rationale: eliminates hash collision risk entirely.
